# internal/tui's HEAVY tests: the ones CI runs in the "tui heavy tests" shards
# instead of the ordinary `go test ./...` job, and that a plain local
# `go test ./...` leaves out. test_schedule_test.go reads this file and is the
# authority on what it means; README.md's "Building and running" says how to
# run them.
#
# One test per line: `<shard> <TopLevelTestName>`. Lines starting with `#` and
# blank lines are ignored; anything else must be exactly those two fields.
#
# THIS IS SCHEDULING, NOT SELECTION. Every top-level test in the package runs in
# exactly one place: the ordinary job skips precisely the names below and shard
# N runs precisely the names marked N, from this one file, so no list can drop a
# test between the two. A name here that stops existing FAILS the ordinary
# suite (TestTestSchedule_EveryHeavyTestIsATopLevelTestHere); a heavy test
# nobody lists runs in the ordinary job, which costs time and never coverage;
# and each shard job fails unless every name marked for it reported a PASS.
#
# WHAT GOES HERE IS DECIDED BY MEASURED COST, not by what kind of test it is.
# Most entries are derived sweeps (every screen at every drawable size), and a
# few are drive tests that type long values through `pump`'s per-key budget.
# The criterion at the time of the split (2026-09-12): at least 3s of wall
# clock on a 14-core machine, or a parallel sweep whose subtests total over 20
# CPU-seconds (those cost several times their local wall clock on CI's 4-core
# runner). Re-measure rather than trusting that:
#
#   SCANTTY_TUI_TESTS=all go test -count=1 -json -timeout 60m ./internal/tui > tui.json
#
# and read each top-level test's run/pass timestamps: the JSON `Elapsed` of a
# test whose subtests call t.Parallel reports 0.
#
# THE SHARD NUMBER only balances the CI jobs; CI derives its matrix from the
# numbers used here, so adding shard 4 adds a job. The three shards were
# balanced to roughly equal estimated cost when the split was made.
